observations:
Torah #272 does not support any package proposals — neither from existing dataset edges (there are none for reference 272) nor from the source text itself.

The source text (5 sentences) is a concentrated practical teaching built around a single idea: serve God one day at a time. Its internal logic is:

1. Opening verse: 'הַיּוֹם אִם בְּקוֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ' — the word 'הַיּוֹם' (today) is the pivot.
2. The ruling: in livelihood AND in avodah, do not plan or worry beyond today.
3. The reason: when one thinks of the full burden of a lifetime of service, it feels unbearable; when one thinks only of today, the burden vanishes.
4. The corollary: do not defer — do not say 'tomorrow I will begin,' 'tomorrow I will pray with proper intention.'
5. The theological ground: tomorrow is a completely different world (עוֹלָם אַחֵר לְגַמְרֵי).

The Rebbe does not invoke bechina relationships at any point. He does not identify any concept as 'an aspect of' another, does not use 'נִקְרָא', does not draw a structural parallel between domains. The phrase 'כְּאִלּוּ הוּא מַשָּׂא כָּבֵד' (it is AS IF a heavy burden) is an explicit simile (כְּאִלּוּ = as if), not a bechina equation. This means no two concepts are claimed to share the same essential nature — the condition required for package formation.

For a package to be proposed, at minimum 2–3 concepts must be linked by explicit 'הוא בחינת' or equivalent language forming an independent domain. Torah #272 contains no such structure. It is a one-concept Torah: live in the present moment of avodah. There is no thematic clustering to represent in graph form for this Torah.
